findings.reason: the plan would either extend the watcher/supervisor edge or state why it cannot, instead of standing up a parallel subsystem on the strength of an unverified absence claim.
findings.text: §7 claims "the design has no push edge at all" and that neither the worker-exit process nor the manifest is "wired", but the tree already has both a per-run supervisor collecting worker exit (`reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`, `reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py`) and a watcher that emits classified run transitions (`watch_ticker` at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:11109`, consumed by `cli.py` `watch_follow`); the section cites neither and names no reason they cannot be extended

findings.reason: the honest change is to make the existing watcher tick deliver the finishing classification it already computes, or to say why a dispatch-scoped wait cannot reuse it; the plan's §2 already routes through the watcher tick, so a second edge is a fork of the path §2 depends on.
findings.text: §7's completion signal adds no classification the follow/watch delivery lacks and gives no justification for a second edge beside it

findings.reason: the finding names the file to extend, so the author can wire the existing supervisor/watcher rather than build a third notification path, and can confirm the territory against the follower plan that already owns the coordinator-facing push.
findings.text: §7 duplicates shared machinery without naming the owner: worker exit is already collected by the per-run supervisor (`fleet_supervisor.py:1` docstring: "per-run supervisors that hold a dispatched worker's parentage so its exit can be collected after its dispatcher is gone"), and terminal-run delivery is owned by `watch_ticker` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:11109`) and the sibling plan `a-follower-keeps-your-work-in-view` §6 ("Push the reader's own obligations"), to which this plan already moved §4

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no spread of shallow wrappers. §3 lands its review record behind one module, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, which hides the content fingerprint, the store keying, the finding-response model and cross-plan recurrence counting behind a small public interface, and explicitly reuses the crew review store root rather than forking one; §2 extends the existing recovery sweep instead of wrapping it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 re-implements a completion/notification edge that already has an owner: the per-run supervisor that "holds a dispatched worker's parentage so its exit can be collected" and the watch ticker that already delivers classified transitions.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2, §3, §4 and §5 are unusually well grounded (each cites the mechanism it extends — recovery.py:145, ticker.py, runs.py:1823, mcp_views.py:967, and §1 carries an explicit reuse-map comment), but §7 — the newest and implementable section — proposes a completion-signal edge while asserting "the design has no push edge at all" and cites no existing mechanism in the tree or a reason none can be extended.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §7's "optional completion signal the orchestrator can wait on" is a thin layer over the classified terminal transitions the watcher/follower already deliver, and the plan does not state why that machinery cannot carry a finishing classification.
